claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires sintering above 2300 °C for full densification.
Adding approximately 5–10 vol% SiC to ZrB2 enables consolidation at about 1700 °C.
SiC promotes lower-temperature consolidation through transient-liquid-assisted liquid-phase sintering.
Transient liquid formation enhances densification of the ZrB2 body.
Transient liquid formation enhances grain-boundary bonding.
The SiC addition produces an in-situ Si-rich intergranular film.
The Si-rich intergranular film transforms during oxidation into a borosilicate-like protective scale.
Si-containing regions preferentially oxidize during service.
The resulting oxide scale is stable and self-healing.
The oxide scale protects underlying ZrB2 from rapid high-temperature oxidation.
The oxide scale protects underlying ZrB2 from corrosion in liquid plating-metal environments.
ZrB2 containing 5–10 vol% SiC and consolidated near 1700 °C will have mechanical strength comparable to or better than ZrB2 consolidated at or above 2300 °C.
The SiC-modified material will retain structural integrity comparable to or better than high-temperature-consolidated single-phase ZrB2.
The SiC-modified material will exhibit significantly greater oxidation resistance than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and earlier lower-temperature specimens.
The SiC-modified material will exhibit less liquid-metal corrosion than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and earlier lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed oxidation protection is expected to operate at temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C.
The proposed protection is expected to operate in molten plating-metal baths.
Outside the stated processing and service bounds, the intended microstructure or protective mechanism may not develop.

contradictions.description: The design specifies only high-temperature pure ZrB2 and low-temperature SiC-doped ZrB2, but the falsification rule requires comparison with an additional non-doped lower-temperature sample. That required control is absent from the stated two-set design.
